criske
comments.body:
@amihaiemil I've found a bug in `BasePaged`. If new projects are registered the total pages will not reflect that increase.
Lets say we have 2 recods initially
```java
Projects projects = storage.projects().page(new Page(1, 2))
projects.totalPages() // should be 1 and is correct
for(int i = 0, i < 10; i++){
  projects.register(...)
}
projects.totalPages()//should be 6 (1 + 5) pages of size 2... but still returns 1
```
I've shoud have kept the `totalRecords` `Supplier` in the old `ProjectsPaged`  https://github.com/self-xdsd/self-core/pull/345/commits/34192ddf2816c7897e981d53c90c9e297811178d

Should I open PR without that test and then create an issue on `self-core`? Or wait for fix?

comments.author: amihaiemil
comments.body: @criske open an Issue in core about it. Also, BasePage should uave the method ``public int totalRecords()``, otherwise it has to be saved in the child class :D

comments.author: amihaiemil
comments.body: @criske can you then take care of this Issue with the cureent approach? .:D

comments.author: criske
comments.body:
> can you then take care of this Issue with the cureent approach? .:D

sure

> open an Issue in core about it. Also, BasePage should uave the method `public int totalRecords()`, otherwise it has to be saved in the child class 

@amihaiemil Maybe I'm wrong, but I don't think we need to expose or especially save `totalRecords`. The database should be our "single source of truth". Any saved snapshots like `totalRecords` in SelfProjects could lead to bad state propagation. Basically pages of SelfProjects should pass `database.jooq().fetchCount()` in order that `totalRecords` from BasePage to be up to date.
Something similar is done in [InMemoryProjects](https://github.com/self-xdsd/self-core/blob/0504426ba8a71524c49b79a5a5fd5c3cbfcd6f83/self-core-impl/src/test/java/com/selfxdsd/core/mock/InMemoryProjects.java#L76)

And I remembered why I ditched the Supplier of totalRecords. Correct me if I'm wrong but `self-storage` will always be queried by `self-web-controllers` in a "stateless" manner, maybe somethin like:
`/projects` -> `storage.projects().page(Page(1, 50)`
`/projects/activate` -> `storage.projects().register(...) ` -> redirect `/projects`
So yeah it's a bug, but in our use case, we can't catch it :D

comments.author: amihaiemil
comments.body: @criske I see. Ok, let's leave it as it is for now:D
